item.title: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide)
item.description:
What it is: NMN (Nicotinamide Mononucleotide) is a precursor to NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide)—a critical coenzyme for cellular energy, DNA repair, and longevity signaling. NMN supplementation restores NAD+ levels that decline with age, activating sirtuins and supporting cellular rejuvenation and aging optimization.

Benefits

Cellular Energy & Mitochondrial Function

  • Restores NAD+ levels (decline ~50% by age 80)
  • Enhances ATP production in mitochondria
  • Improves mitochondrial function
  • Supports cellular energy metabolism
  • Reduces fatigue and improves vitality

Longevity & Anti-Aging Pathways

  • Activates sirtuins (longevity genes)
  • Supports cellular rejuvenation
  • Activates autophagy and cellular cleanup
  • Extends lifespan in animal models 10-30%
  • Reverses aging markers in research

NAD+-Dependent DNA Repair

  • NAD+ essential for DNA repair (PARPs)
  • Supports genomic stability
  • Protects against DNA damage
  • Reduces cancer risk (theoretical)
  • Supports healthy aging

Cardiovascular & Metabolic Health

  • Supports endothelial function
  • Improves vascular health
  • Supports metabolic health
  • May improve insulin sensitivity
  • Blood pressure regulation support

Cognitive Function & Neuroprotection

  • Crosses blood-brain barrier
  • Supports neuronal mitochondria
  • Neuroprotective effects
  • Supports cognitive aging
  • May reduce neurodegeneration risk

Dosage

General longevity: 250-500 mg daily Enhanced anti-aging: 500-750 mg daily Full spectrum: 750-1,000 mg daily Timing: Morning with breakfast Duration: Minimum 12 weeks before assessing; benefits build over time

item.title: L-Carnitine
item.description:
What it is: L-Carnitine is a naturally occurring amino acid that transports long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria for oxidation into energy. Essential for fat metabolism and ATP production, it’s particularly valuable for athletes, aging populations, and those optimizing body composition without the stimulant side effects of other fat-loss supplements.

What Is L-Carnitine?

L-Carnitine is a quaternary amine compound synthesized in the body from amino acids lysine and methionine. While your body produces carnitine naturally (about 1-2 grams daily), dietary sources are limited, and supplementation can increase carnitine availability significantly—particularly for those with high metabolic demands.

item.title: Spermidine
item.description:
What it is: Spermidine is a natural polyamine that activates autophagy—the cellular “cleaning” process that removes damaged components and rejuvenates cells. Emerging longevity research suggests spermidine supplementation extends lifespan in animal models and improves cardiovascular health in human studies, making it one of the most promising natural longevity compounds.

What Is Spermidine?

Spermidine is an organic compound found naturally throughout the body and in some foods (aged cheese, mushrooms, legumes, whole grains). It plays crucial roles in cell division, protein synthesis, and—most importantly for longevity—autophagy regulation.

item.title: Energy Production: How Your Body Creates ATP
item.description:
How Energy Production Works

Your body converts food into usable energy through a sophisticated system of biochemical reactions. The fundamental unit of energy in your body is ATP (adenosine triphosphate), a small molecule that stores energy in its chemical bonds.

The Three Stages of Energy Production

1. Glycolysis (Cytoplasm)

  • Glucose (or amino acids/fatty acids) enters the cytoplasm
  • Broken down into 2 pyruvate molecules
  • Produces a net of 2 ATP molecules and 2 NADH
  • Does NOT require oxygen (anaerobic)
  • Fast energy source, useful for explosive activities

2. Citric Acid Cycle (Mitochondrial Matrix)

item.title: Vitamin B3 (Niacin)
item.description:
What Is Vitamin B3 (Niacin)?

Vitamin B3, also known as niacin, nicotinic acid, or vitamin PP (pellagra-preventing), exists as multiple chemical entities with different biochemical functions and biohacking implications. Understanding these distinctions is critical for optimizing outcomes:

Nicotinic Acid (Niacin): The original form recognized to prevent pellagra (severe deficiency disease); provides the flush response and most potent therapeutic effects on lipid profiles and NAD+ elevation.

Nicotinamide (Niacinamide): The non-flushing form; functions as a direct NAD+ precursor but lacks the lipid-modifying and flushing effects of nicotinic acid—important distinction for protocol selection.
